title: The light switch's own fuse needs a wire, and the column connectors …
ask: Block 00.30 gave the light switch its own fuse, but every wire position to the steering column is taken. Which way does it get its own supply?
why: You chose (a) for block 00.30: split F3 and hold state on a fault. The fuse and the logic halves are done. The wake stages have their own 3 A fuse, F23. Ignition and the headlamps now hold their state if their switch's reading faults, including when its fuse blows. One part is left. The ignition switch and the light switch are both fed by one wire, L3-S2 2, which splits behind the steering column, and the brake-pedal wake switch hangs off it too. Giving the light switch its own fuse at the dash node needs a second wire to the column. All 24 positions in the column connectors (L3-S1, L3-S2) are used. The only unused ones in the leg are L3-S3 1-3, the three capped radar pass-throughs, and the radar is still open as block 01.11. Until this is answered, a short on the light-switch side blows the key's fuse. The engine and headlamps now hold through that, but it is still the one fuse.
options:
(a) A fuse in the branch. Keep the one wire and put a 3 A sealed inline fuse where the light-switch and brake-switch branch leaves it, behind the column. A short on the light side then blows only that fuse. About $5, no connector change. The fuse sits behind the lower dash panel, not at the dash node with the others.
(b) Borrow a radar pass-through. L3-S3 1 becomes the light switch's own wire, from a new fuse at the dash node. The two supplies are fully separate and every fuse is in one place. The radar (block 01.11) keeps two pass-throughs instead of three.
(c) One more small connector. Add a 2-way sealed connector (a DTM-2 pair) to the column leg for the new wire, from a new fuse at the dash node. The supplies are fully separate and the radar keeps all three. About $10, and one more connector to seal and label.
recommend: (a), unless the radar in block 01.11 turns out to need fewer than three pass-throughs, then (b). The new hold logic already covers the key fuse blowing; what is left is a light-side short taking the key fuse with it, and (a) fixes exactly that for about five dollars.
stops: The light-switch half of R2: the fuses table, one wire or splice in the L3 leg, and the fuse-holder count on the cart. Nothing already bought changes.

title: When the new wiring goes in: all at once, or one circuit at a time?
ask: When the new harness is installed, after the design is frozen, do you move every circuit over in one stretch, or keep the car starting on its old wiring while circuits move one at a time?
why: Your answer to block 00.29 was: "car currently does not start, broke down no wireing changes have been made". Understood. The breakdown is recorded as a car issue (K-025). This question is not about the car today. It is about install steps E26 to E28, months from now, after the design is frozen and the parts are bought. At E26 the key and the column switches (lights, turn, wipers, hazard) are rewired as signals into the new PMU, and from then on they cannot also run the old wiring. The install plan assumes the old wiring still starts the car through those weeks, and it cannot. The interior is out for the whole build (D-387), so the car is not driven during the install either way. The only question is whether it should still start.
options:
(a) All at once. Plug in the new column wiring and move every circuit over in one stretch (E26 to E28 back to back), using the migration table as the test order. Nothing extra to buy. The car does not start until the last circuit has moved, and a fault found late is found with everything already moved.
(b) Lights and motors first, switches last. The old key and switches keep running the old wiring while each light and motor moves over one at a time. Each moved circuit is tested from a temporary box of toggle switches (about 30 dollars), and the real switches move last. The car keeps starting on its old wiring until that last step.
recommend: (a), unless you want the car to keep starting on its old wiring through the install weeks. It has fewer temporary wires to get wrong and costs nothing.
stops: The wording of install steps E26 to E28 and the migration table (R1). Nothing already bought changes.
